$comment: Subject Vocabulary Standard 0.9, a pre-release for testing before 1.0. SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0. Copyright 2026 Jamie Clayton. 0.x versions may still change within their folder; from 1.0, released versions are immutable and changes ship as a new major.minor folder. Rules that JSON Schema cannot express (SV001 onwards) are defined in the specification and checked by conformance tooling. The concept shape follows W3C SKOS; see context.jsonld.
title: Subject vocabulary core scheme
description: The core scheme the standard publishes: the abilities every adopting repository shares, each a SKOS concept carried in Dublin Core subject as ability:<name>. Repositories pin it in their adoption register and either extend it with their own concepts or replace it with a private set; ability: notations always mean this scheme. Its $defs also define the concept shape the adoption register and the suggestions file reuse.

$schema.description: The released version of this standard the scheme conforms to (dcterms:conformsTo).

identifier.description: Persistent identifier of the scheme, as a URI (dcterms:identifier).

created.description: When the scheme was first created (dcterms:created).

language.description: BCP 47 language tag for labels and definitions (dcterms:language).

rights.description: Licence of the scheme, ideally an SPDX identifier (dcterms:rights).

retired.description: Concepts no longer offered, each naming its replacement.

dateOrDateTime.description: A calendar date, or a date-time with an explicit offset. A date-time without an offset is rejected because it is ambiguous.

notation.description: The token written in front-matter subject (skos:notation): a scheme prefix, a colon, and a lowercase name. ability: is reserved for the core scheme; local concepts use a prefix their register declares (theme: and component: by default). SV004 checks which prefix belongs where.

label.description: A label or hint, matched as a literal string, never as a pattern.

conceptBody.description: Every key a concept may carry. coreConcept and the adoption register's localConcept each say which are required.

definition.description: The promise the concept makes to the person using the product (skos:definition).

scopeNote.description: What is in and out of scope, naming the nearest neighbour (skos:scopeNote).

audience.description: Whether customer-facing views show the concept (dcterms:audience).

altLabel.description: Other names for the concept, including names it absorbed; a strong suggester signal (skos:altLabel).

hiddenLabel.description: Hints for the suggester, never displayed (skos:hiddenLabel).

related.description: Concepts that often travel with this one (skos:related).

exactMatch.description: Concepts in other schemes with the same meaning (skos:exactMatch). An entry with scheme core names an ability: concept of the pinned core scheme: a local concept that exact-matches a core ability groups with it across repositories.

closeMatch.description: Comparable concepts in other schemes (skos:closeMatch). Shown beside a core ability, never counted in it. Cite a characteristic's name, never another standard's text.

scheme.description: The other scheme; core means this standard's pinned core scheme.

coreConcept.$comment: Shapes come from conceptBody; the true entries only declare which keys are required here.

retiredConcept.description: A concept no longer offered. deprecatedAt to removedAt is its validity window (dcterms:valid).

isReplacedBy.description: The active concept to use instead (dcterms:isReplacedBy).

extensions.description: Repository-specific data the standard does not define, kept apart so every other key stays strictly checked. Any keys and values. Consumers that do not understand an extension ignore it.
